Jade.et: From French jade (“jade”), rebracketing of earlier l'ejade (“jade”), from Spanish piedra de ijada (“flank stone”), from Vulgar Latin *iliata, from Latin ilia (“flank”) (Jade was thought to cure pains in the side).

s: emphatic yes, used especially when someone asks the same question repeatedly
Und du bist dir auch wirklich sicher? – Ja doch! Ich sage dir doch, ich habe es mit eigenen Augen gesehen!
So you’re really sure? – Yes! I’ve been telling you, I saw it with my own eyes!
expresses annoyance at a repeated question or a request, often translatable as come on
Und du hast ganz sicher die Schlüssel eingesteckt? – Ja doch, wie oft soll ich's denn noch sagen?
And are you absolutely sure you’ve pocketed the keys? - Come on, how many more times do I have to say it?
Jetzt beeil dich doch, wir kommen zu spät! – Ja doch, ich bin ja eh gleich fertig!
Hurry up now, we’re going to be late! - Oh, come on, I’ll be done in a minute.
